subject.title: RFC 0024: Localization Runtime and Product Coverage

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor RFC 0024 as the shared localization architecture across Gateway, CLI, channels, command metadata, plugins, and release coverage despite the earlier not-planned product direction?
rationale: The repository cannot infer acceptance because the RFC intentionally creates cross-owner product and compatibility contracts, while prior discussion declined a broader localization program.

options.title: Complete owner review
options.body: Keep the RFC draft and require explicit Gateway, channels/product, command-catalog, plugin/package, and release-owner decisions before acceptance.

options.title: Narrow the first contract
options.body: Limit this RFC to locale resolution and compatibility-preserving message descriptors, deferring metadata APIs and release gates to later RFCs.

options.title: Retain prior direction
options.body: Decline the product-wide architecture if no owner group is prepared to sponsor and implement the staged program.

recommendation.title: Complete owner review
recommendation.body: Keep the RFC draft and require explicit Gateway, channels/product, command-catalog, plugin/package, and release-owner decisions before acceptance.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior pinned product-direction response makes this person the clearest available owner for deciding whether the localization strategy should change.
